# Upper control arm and coil bucket contact

## Summary

[Partial] Inspect upper control arms and measure contact depth to determine if grinding is needed. [t828]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Inspect the upper control arms (UCA) for a clean cut where they hit the coil bucket.
2. [Partial] Measure the depth of the contact mark, which is often about 1/32 of an inch deep.

_Procedure reported by [t828]._

## Parts

- [Partial] Aftermarket Upper Control Arms: Tube design that slides around the bucket rather than hitting it [t828]
- [Partial] Grinding tool or file: To remove the lip on the coil bucket if not replacing UCAs [t828]

## Tips & gotchas

- Look for UCA designs that 'slide around' the bucket instead of hitting it directly. [t828]
- [Partial] If keeping stock arms, grind down the small lip on the top of the coil bucket. [t828]
